newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end up but off highs.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end up but off highs.

text.p: Singapore shares ended up, but off their highs on Monday in dealings made cautious by a perceived weakness in Malaysian issues traded over the counter despite firm market sentiment, dealers said.
"Prices were mostly moving within a range for most of the day. Though there was some buying of blue chips, the volume was not really convincing," said one.
The Straits Times Industrial index eased from the day's high of 2,041.22 to 2,028.68, up 12.37 points.
Total market volume was 128.15 million shares with 207 gainers against 131 losers.
Singapore Telecom shares rose three cents to end at S$2.43 with more than 3.4 million shares traded.

One analyst said there was some bargain hunting of the stock because SingTel still had the lion's share of the Singapore telecoms market despite losing its monopoly on April 1, which sent its shares into a sharp fall.
Electronics-based Uraco ended at 88 cents, down seven cents, with more than 3.3 million traded in speculative trading.
Gainers included City Developments, Keppel Corp and UOB foreign, while SIA foreign and OUUB foreign ended weaker.
